name: Phos
subtitle: Read first. Scroll later.
promotionalText: Start the day in the Word. Phos keeps social media locked until you read today's chapter, reflect on it, and answer a few questions about it.
description:
Phos is Greek for light. It keeps your most distracting apps locked each morning until you have spent time in the Bible.

HOW IT WORKS
• Choose the apps that pull you in, like social media and video.
• Each morning they lock at the time you pick.
• Read today's chapter in your own Bible, read it in Phos, or listen to it.
• Reflect by typing or speaking about what stood out. Paste is turned off.
• Answer a few questions written for that exact chapter.
• Your apps open for as long as you choose.

QUESTIONS THAT PROVE YOU READ IT
Over 4,600 questions cover the whole New Testament, Genesis, Psalms, and Proverbs. Multiple choice, fill in the blank phrases, put events in order, and true or false. They range from fair to genuinely challenging, and if you truly read the chapter, you will know the answers. Miss too many and Phos shows you the verses you missed, then lets you try new questions after a short wait.

REFLECTION, NOT BUSYWORK
Type your thoughts, say them out loud, or answer three short prompts. Phos only counts the seconds you are actually talking, and checks that your reflection is really about the chapter. Everything you write is saved to your private journal.

LATER IN THE DAY
When your open time ends, one quick question brings your apps back. Midday questions can quote what you wrote that morning. You can also unlock with a focus session with your phone face down, or by reciting the chapter's key verse from memory.

YOUR RULES
Every rule is yours to set: words to type, seconds of talking, reading time, number of questions, how many you need right, and how long apps stay open, from five minutes to the rest of the day. Stricter changes apply right away. Easier changes wait a day, so a tired moment cannot undo your plan.

ALSO INCLUDED
• Reading plans: John, Mark, Matthew, Luke, Acts, Paul's letters, the New Testament, Genesis, Psalms, and Proverbs
• Plan card, reading path, and calendar views
• Streaks, weekly Screen Time trends, and a reflection journal
• The full World English Bible with the words of Jesus in red
• Read aloud
• Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets
• Three emergency passes a month, and Phone, Messages, and Maps are never locked
• Morning, midday, and evening schedules

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
No account, no ads, no tracking, no servers. Apple's Screen Time keeps your app choices private, even from Phos, and your reflections never leave your iPhone.

“Your word is a lamp to my feet, and a light for my path.” Psalm 119:105
reviewNotes:
No account or sign in is required.

Phos uses the Family Controls framework with individual authorization so a person can lock their own distracting apps until they finish a daily Bible reading.

To test the full flow:
1. Open Phos and go through setup. Tap Allow Screen Time access and approve with Face ID or passcode.
2. Tap Choose apps to lock and pick any app, for example Safari or a game.
3. Pick the Gospel of John plan and finish setup. The chosen app is now locked. Opening it shows the Phos lock screen.
4. On that lock screen tap the unlock button. Apple does not allow a shield to open another app, so Phos posts a local notification. Tap it to open Phos.
5. Tap Start reading, choose Read in Phos to read John 1 inside the app. During the first 24 hours after setup every rule change applies instantly, so you can set Minimum reading time to Off and Words to type to 20 under Settings, Unlock rules, to move faster.
6. Type a short reflection about John 1 (mention John the Baptist, the Word, or the light), then answer the questions. Three correct answers unlock the apps for the chosen time.

Other features: speaking a reflection uses the microphone and on device speech recognition. Focus session reads device motion to confirm the phone is face down. The weekly chart uses a DeviceActivityReport extension. Nothing leaves the device.

Bible text is the World English Bible, which is in the public domain.
